report.title: Anthropic ships 10 finance agent templates and Claude Opus 4.7
report.summary: Anthropic released 10 ready-to-run agent templates for pitchbook creation, KYC screening, and month-end close alongside Claude Opus 4.7, which leads Vals AI's Finance Agent benchmark at 64.37%. Templates deploy as Claude Code plugins or headless Managed Agents via API, with full Microsoft 365 add-in support (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook). JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon appeared on stage at the NYC launch event.

report.title: OpenAI ships GPT-Realtime-2 with GPT-5-class reasoning and two companion voice models
report.summary: OpenAI released three new Realtime API models on May 7: GPT-Realtime-2 (GPT-5-class reasoning, 128K context, adjustable effort), GPT-Realtime-Translate (70+ input languages, 13 output), and GPT-Realtime-Whisper (streaming STT at $0.017/min). Collapses the stitched-together transcription+reasoning+synthesis stack into a single API surface. Zillow reported a 26-point lift in call-success rate in early testing.

report.title: OpenAI makes GPT-5.5 Instant the new default for all ChatGPT users
report.summary: GPT-5.5 Instant replaced GPT-5.3 Instant as ChatGPT's default model on May 5, with 52.5% fewer hallucinated claims on high-stakes prompts per internal evals and improved personalization from past chats, Gmail, and uploaded files. Available in the API as chat-latest; GPT-5.3 Instant stays accessible to paid users for three more months before retirement.

report.title: Anthropic opens Claude Managed Agents multiagent and Outcomes to public beta
report.summary: The Claude Developer Platform expanded Managed Agents to include multiagent sessions and rubric-based Outcomes in public beta under the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header, plus webhook support for session and vault lifecycle events. Builders can now coordinate sub-agents and evaluate work against defined criteria without building their own orchestration layer.

report.title: Anthropic doubles Claude Code rate limits after SpaceX compute deal closes
report.summary: Anthropic doubled five-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise Claude Code tiers and removed peak-hour reductions for Pro and Max, crediting a new compute partnership with SpaceX that taps xAI's Colossus supercomputer. Opus API limits also raised. Effective immediately with no plan changes required.

report.title: Anthropic's Mythos model triggers US government pre-release AI review expansion
report.summary: Google, Microsoft, and xAI agreed to give the US Commerce Department's CAISI early access to models for national security evaluation, joining existing Anthropic and OpenAI partnerships — prompted largely by concern over Anthropic's unreleased Mythos model, which Anthropic says is far ahead of other models in cybersecurity capability and is restricted to approved organizations only.

report.title: EU AI Act high-risk compliance deadline pushed from August 2026 to December 2027
report.summary: EU negotiators struck a deal extending enforcement of high-risk AI rules by 16 months, giving companies deploying AI in hiring, lending, healthcare, education, and law enforcement substantially more runway. Teams that had been racing Q3 2026 compliance roadmaps can now reprioritize.

learn.name: Claude Agent SDK (Python)
learn.oneLineDescription: Python SDK that wraps Claude's tool-execution loop — write agents without building the loop yourself.

detail.whatItDoes:
The Claude Agent SDK is Anthropic's Python library that gives you Claude with built-in tool execution. Unlike the raw Anthropic client where you implement the tool loop yourself, the Agent SDK handles the full agentic loop: Claude reasons, decides which tools to call, executes them (Bash, file I/O, glob, web fetch, etc.), and iterates until the task is done. You stream results back with an async generator. The SDK requires the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header, which it sets automatically.

As of this week the SDK is in public beta, and multiagent sessions and Outcomes (rubric-based task evaluation) are available for early access. The same core capability powers Claude Code; the SDK exposes it for teams building their own branded agents on top of Claude infrastructure.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers building autonomous coding agents, research pipelines, or document-processing workflows. Also relevant for teams that want to ship Claude-powered products without maintaining their own tool-execution scaffolding. The SDK is a good fit any time your task requires file reads, shell commands, or multi-step iteration rather than a single prompt-response round trip.
pros: No tool loop to maintain — Claude handles retries, tool dispatch, and context management internally
Drop-in compatibility with Claude Code workflows; CLI sessions and SDK sessions share the same permission model and skill files
Multiagent support in public beta: one orchestrator can spin up sub-agents and aggregate results
Streams results incrementally, so long-running tasks don't block
Outcomes API lets you evaluate agent work against a rubric without writing your own eval harness
cons: All Managed Agents endpoints require the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header; forgetting it returns a 400 error that can be confusing
Multiagent and Outcomes are still in research preview — behaviors may change between releases
Agent SDK costs more per task than a raw client call because the model handles multiple tool rounds internally; budget token use carefully for high-volume workloads
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- An Anthropic API key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in your environment)
- The beta header is handled automatically by the SDK, but note you must be on a **Team, Enterprise, or API plan** to access Managed Agents endpoints.

## Install

```bash
pip install claude-agent-sdk
```

## Minimal working agent

```python
import asyncio
from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions

async def main():
    async for message in query(
        prompt="List every Python file in the current directory and print the first 5 lines of each.",
        options=ClaudeAgentOptions(
            allowed_tools=["Bash", "Glob", "Read"]
        ),
    ):
        if hasattr(message, "result"):
            print(message.result)

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Run with an explicit model

```python
from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions

options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-5",          # or claude-opus-4-7 for heavier tasks
    allowed_tools=["Bash", "Read", "Write"],
    max_turns=20,                        # cap iterations to control cost
)

async def run(prompt: str):
    async for msg in query(prompt=prompt, options=options):
        print(msg)
```

## Gotcha: beta header
The SDK sets `anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01` automatically. If you're hitting a raw API endpoint alongside the SDK (e.g., for logging), **you must add this header manually** or the Managed Agents endpoint will return 400.

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
client.beta = "managed-agents-2026-04-01"  # raw client path
```

## Docs
Full reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview

learn.name: oMLX
learn.oneLineDescription: Local LLM inference server for Apple Silicon with SSD KV-cache and a macOS menu bar UI.

detail.whatItDoes:
oMLX is a Python-based LLM inference server purpose-built for Apple Silicon (M1–M4). It runs on top of the MLX framework and implements continuous batching and a two-tier KV cache: a hot in-memory tier and a cold SSD tier. KV cache persists across sessions and context changes, so long multi-turn coding sessions with tools like Claude Code don't pay the full prefill cost on every request. The server exposes an OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible REST API on localhost:8000, so any client that points at those endpoints (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline) works with zero reconfiguration.

The menu bar app lets you pin frequently used models in memory, auto-swap heavier models on demand, and monitor memory usage without opening a terminal. A web admin dashboard at /admin provides chat, benchmarks, and per-model settings. Supported model types include text LLMs, vision-language models (VLMs), OCR models, embeddings, and rerankers.
detail.whoItsFor: Mac developers who want local inference for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) without paying API costs or sending data to the cloud. Also useful for teams that need offline operation, GDPR compliance, or reproducible inference across low-latency agentic loops. Requires macOS 15 Sequoia and Apple Silicon; not relevant on Intel Macs or non-Apple hardware.
pros: Two-tier KV cache (RAM + SSD) makes long coding-agent sessions fast — context stays cached across requests even when conversation changes
OpenAI and Anthropic API compatibility means any agent tool works with zero reconfiguration
Menu bar UI eliminates terminal management for model loading, pinning, and memory monitoring
Supports multi-model serving with LRU eviction — pin small everyday models, auto-load larger ones on demand
Fully offline after model download; all CDN dependencies vendored
cons: macOS 15 Sequoia and Apple Silicon required — no Linux, no Intel, no Windows
Benchmark numbers show slightly higher latency versus other inference engines because the cache snapshot overhead is tuned for agent reuse patterns, not single-shot throughput
VLM continuous batching requires a recent mlx-vlm build; older pinned versions may not support it
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS 15.0+ (Sequoia)
- Apple Silicon (M1, M2, M3, or M4)
- Python 3.10+ (Homebrew path: `brew install python@3.12` recommended)
- Homebrew (https://brew.sh)

## Install via Homebrew (recommended for CLI usage)

```bash
brew tap jundot/omlx https://github.com/jundot/omlx
brew install omlx

# Run as a background service that auto-restarts on crash
brew services start omlx
```

## OR: Install as a macOS app (menu bar UI)

1. Download the `.dmg` from https://github.com/jundot/omlx/releases
2. Drag `oMLX.app` to `/Applications`
3. Launch it — the Welcome screen walks you through setting a model directory and downloading your first model.

The app includes in-app auto-update; future upgrades are one click. Note: the macOS app does **not** install the `omlx` CLI. If you need both, install the app AND run the Homebrew step.

## Download a model and start the server

```bash
# Point oMLX at a directory of MLX-format model subdirectories
omlx serve --model-dir ~/models

# Or persist the path so you don't need the flag every time
omlx serve --model-dir ~/models  # writes ~/.omlx/settings.json
omlx serve                        # next run uses saved settings
```

Models must be in MLX format. Download from Hugging Face:

```bash
# Example: download Qwen3-Coder (8-bit quantized) with the HF CLI
pip install huggingface_hub
huggingface-cli download mlx-community/Qwen3-Coder-Next-8bit \
  --local-dir ~/models/Qwen3-Coder-Next-8bit
```

## Connect Claude Code to oMLX

```bash
# oMLX provides a one-command launcher that sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL,
# ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, and execs Claude Code with the selected model
omlx launch claude
```

This opens a minimal TUI listing loaded models; pick one, press Enter, and Claude Code starts pointing at your local server.

## Verify the server is running

```bash
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/models
# Should return JSON listing all discovered models
```

Admin dashboard (chat, benchmark, monitoring): http://localhost:8000/admin

## Gotcha: MCP support is opt-in
MCP (Model Context Protocol) is not installed by default. Add it:

```bash
# Homebrew install path
/opt/homebrew/opt/omlx/libexec/bin/pip install mcp

# Source install
pip install -e ".[mcp]"
```

learn.name: OpenAI Realtime API (GPT-Realtime-2)
learn.oneLineDescription: GPT-5-class speech-to-speech API with 128K context, tool calling, and real-time translation in one endpoint.

detail.whatItDoes:
The OpenAI Realtime API now includes three new models released May 7, 2026. GPT-Realtime-2 is the flagship: a speech-to-speech model with GPT-5-class reasoning, a 128K token context window (up from 32K), adjustable reasoning effort (minimal to xhigh), parallel tool calling, and built-in recovery from interruptions. It keeps the conversation moving while it calls tools, emitting a preamble (e.g. 'let me check that') so users don't sit in silence. GPT-Realtime-Translate handles live speech translation across 70+ input languages into 13 output languages at $0.034/min. GPT-Realtime-Whisper provides streaming speech-to-text at $0.017/min for live captions and meeting notes.

All three models live in the Realtime API and Playground. They replace the stitched-together stack (Whisper + ElevenLabs + your own reasoning hop) that most voice agent teams were running, collapsing it into one API call with one billing line.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers building voice agents, customer support bots, live transcription services, or multilingual products. GPT-Realtime-2 is the right default for any voice agent that needs to call tools or handle complex requests. GPT-Realtime-Translate targets cross-border support and global education platforms. GPT-Realtime-Whisper fits live captioning, healthcare documentation, and post-call summarization pipelines.
pros: 128K context window enables long agentic voice sessions without external state stitching
Single API replaces a 3-component stack (transcription + reasoning + synthesis), reducing latency and ops complexity
Parallel tool calls with preambles eliminate dead-air pauses during tool execution
GPT-Realtime-Translate at $0.034/min undercuts most competing translation services
EU Data Residency supported for GDPR-constrained deployments
cons: GPT-Realtime-2 is billed by audio tokens ($32/1M input, $64/1M output) — high-volume call centers should model costs carefully before migrating from per-minute pricing
Output language coverage for Translate is limited to 13 languages despite 70+ input languages — niche language pairs still require alternatives
Adjustable reasoning effort defaults to 'low'; xhigh effort adds latency that may feel unnatural in fast conversational turns

learn.name: Claude Code Auto Mode
learn.oneLineDescription: Runs multi-step Claude Code sessions without per-action approval prompts, using a two-stage safety classifier.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Code Auto Mode, launched in late March 2026 and now generally available, removes the per-action approval prompts that previously interrupted long coding sessions. A two-stage classifier evaluates each proposed action before execution: a fast initial filter passes obviously safe operations (reading files, running tests) instantly, while ambiguous or high-impact operations (modifying production configs, pushing to remote branches) escalate to deeper analysis and may still pause for human approval. The spinner turns red when a permission check fires, giving a clear visual signal.

Auto Mode is distinct from fully disabling permissions (--dangerously-skip-permissions). It does not bypass safety checks; it automates the routine approval decisions while preserving gates for sensitive operations. Enterprise admins can disable it org-wide via managed settings. Hard deny rules, introduced in the latest Claude Code update, let teams block specific operation classes even in Auto Mode.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers running large refactors, migrations, or long exploratory tasks where repeated approval dialogs break flow. Also relevant for CI/CD pipelines where Claude Code runs headless on scheduled tasks via Dispatch. Enterprise teams with compliance requirements should use managed settings to configure Auto Mode org-wide rather than leaving it to individual users.
pros: Eliminates approval fatigue on safe operations without giving up safety gates on high-impact actions
Visual feedback (red spinner) makes it clear when Auto Mode is pausing for a real approval — not silent
Hard deny rules let teams permanently block operation classes (e.g. remote git pushes) regardless of Auto Mode state
Works with Claude Sonnet 4.5 (default) and Opus 4.6/4.7 — no model-specific setup needed
Enterprise admins can disable it organization-wide with a single managed settings key
cons: Still a research preview for some multi-agent sub-agent workflows — behavior may be refined
Auto Mode does not cover every scenario; some operations the classifier is uncertain about will still interrupt you
AutoDream tasks run 10–20 classifier steps per complex prompt, which adds token overhead on long sessions
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Claude Code installed: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` (v2.1+)
- An Anthropic API key or a Claude Pro/Team/Enterprise plan
- Update to the latest version: `claude update`

## Enable Auto Mode

**From the CLI:**

```bash
claude --enable-auto-mode
```

**Toggle mid-session:**
Press `Shift+Tab` to toggle Auto Mode on or off inside a running Claude Code session.

**From VS Code extension:**
Open Claude Code sidebar → Settings → Enable Auto Mode.

## Verify Auto Mode is active

```bash
claude --status
# Should show: Auto Mode: enabled
```

When active, watch the spinner in the top-left of the terminal panel. It turns **red** when a permission check fires and Auto Mode is pausing for approval.

## Set hard deny rules (block specific operations regardless of Auto Mode)

Create or edit `.claude/settings.json` in your project root:

```json
{
  "autoMode": {
    "hardDenyRules": [
      { "tool": "Bash", "pattern": "git push" },
      { "tool": "Bash", "pattern": "rm -rf" }
    ]
  }
}
```

These rules apply even when `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is set.

## Disable org-wide (Enterprise admins)

In your organization's managed settings JSON (configured via Claude Console):

```json
{
  "disableAutoMode": "disable"
}
```

This prevents any user in the org from enabling Auto Mode, regardless of local settings.

## Gotcha: OAuth + CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS
If your deployment sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1`, older versions had a bug where OAuth auth entered a 401 retry loop when Auto Mode was active. Update to v2.1.128+ to get the fix:

```bash
claude update
```

## Docs
https://www.anthropic.com/news/enabling-claude-code-to-work-more-autonomously
